column1: What does an ExternalName Service actually do?
column2: Returns a DNS CNAME record pointing to an external hostname — pure DNS redirection, no proxying, no ClusterIP, no kube-proxy involvement

column1: Does an ExternalName Service have any EndpointSlices?
column2: No — it never creates endpoints of any kind, unlike both ClusterIP and selectorless Services

column1: Can externalName be set to an IP address?
column2: No — it's treated as a DNS name made of digits, not an IP, and fails to resolve (NXDOMAIN)

column1: What happens if you add a selector field to an ExternalName Service?
column2: Nothing — it's accepted by the API but has zero effect; ExternalName remains pure DNS redirection regardless

column1: What Host header does an external server see when accessed via ExternalName?
column2: Your internal Service's own name, not the external server's real hostname — can cause rejections on Host-header-strict servers

column1: Can an ExternalName Service's externalName point at another Kubernetes Service's own DNS name?
column2: Yes — CNAME chaining to a real resolvable hostname works, including another ClusterIP Service's internal DNS name

column1: What's the main practical value of using ExternalName instead of hardcoding a hostname in application config?
column2: If the external target changes, you update one Service object instead of every deployment's config — the app always talks to a stable internal name

column1: When would you use a selectorless Service instead of ExternalName?
column2: When your external target is a stable IP address (not a hostname) and you need port mapping or load balancing across multiple IPs — covered in 02-service-internals

column1: Does ExternalName perform any load balancing?
column2: No — it returns a single CNAME; any load balancing happens at the external DNS level if that hostname has multiple A records

column1: Is kubectl create service externalname the same command family as kubectl expose?
column2: No — kubectl expose has no ExternalName mode; ExternalName Services use the separate kubectl create service externalname subcommand
